subject: Acme: Post-call integration & model-routing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Acme: Post-call integration & model-routing next steps

Hi Sarah — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so your team can share internally. TL;DR: SDK auth + routing prototype, a short eval with embeddings+reranker, and a model-routing policy design to meet your latency/cost constraints.

Key notes from the call:
- Integration scope: live inference for customer support triage (chat + semantic search) and an offline batch reranking job for weekly digest.
- Data residency: production traffic must stay in us-east for now; some analytics can use eu-west.
- SLOs: p95 latency target of 250ms for chat (short prompts), cost target: keep token cost under $0.003/1000 tokens for bulk rerank paths.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We (Redwood) ship a small SDK example repo and auth guide so your infra team can spin up a local dev loop (Dev to own).
2) Marcus to propose a model-routing policy: primary low-latency model for chat, fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized variant during load, and region routing for eu-west analytics.
3) Run a short eval using your sample queries to test embeddings + reranker config and measure recall/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: acme-redwood-mapping-design.pdf (integration sketch), redwood-sdk-setup-guide.md (quick auth + SDK snippets).

Do you want us to schedule a technical walkthrough (30m) with your infra and security folks next week? If so, share 2 slots that work for you.

Thanks,
Marissa

2) Security: our security team will want an overview of auth (OIDC + service accounts) and audit logging for inference requests. Can you include that in the walkthrough?

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call integration & model-routing next steps

Sarah — quick answers and what we'll bring to the tech walkthrough: 

Embeddings + Reranker:
- Default starting point: open embedding model "redwood-embed-compact-v1" for semantic search paired with a small candidate reranker using cross-encoder "redwood-rank-small-v1" for the weekly digest. That combo gives good precision@5 with modest cost.
- We'll include a short eval harness and example prompts to measure recall/precision and token costs.

SDK + Auth:
- SDK snippets in redwood-sdk-setup-guide.md show OIDC service account flow + short-lived tokens. We support both API key for quick eval and OpenID Connect for production.
- Audit logs: per-request metadata (request_id, model, routing_policy, user_id) can be exported to your SIEM via CloudWatch/Stackdriver; we'll document required fields.

Model routing + policy (high level):
- Primary route: low-latency model (e.g. "redwood-gen-lowlatency-v2") in us-east for chat; p95 ~ 180–220ms under typical load.
- Fallback chain: if queue depth exceeds threshold or p95 breaching, route to quantized variant "redwood-gen-q8-lite" (cost ~40% lower) or to Dedicated reserved pool if available.
- Cost policies: per-route cost cap that switches to cheaper model after cumulative token spend threshold per hour/day (helps control runaway costs during events).
- Region routing: eu-west traffic (analytics) routed to regional instance configured with identical policy but using eu-hosted models.

What we'll bring to the walkthrough:
- A short live demo of SDK auth and a routing policy toggle in the Console.
- A sample eval run showing embeddings + reranker precision@5 and latency histogram.
- A draft routing policy YAML and sequence diagram (we'll attach before the meeting).

I can take the walkthrough on Wed 11/25 14:00 PT with Marcus joining for policy details.

Cheers,
Dev
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme: Post-call integration & model-routing next steps

Sarah — adding the routing policy sketch and a few decision points so you can review ahead of Wed's walkthrough: 

Routing policy sketch (summary):
- Route name: acme-support-primary
- Criteria: request.type == "chat" && request.avg_input_tokens < 512 && client_region == "us-east" -> route to redwood-gen-lowlatency-v2
- Fallbacks: if p95_latency_window_1m > 300ms OR queue_length > 80 -> route to redwood-gen-q8-lite
- Cost guardrail: if cost_1h > $X then degrade non-essential paths (batch rerank) to cheaper models or pause non-critical background reranks.
- Embedding pipeline: nearest-neighbor store in your vector DB (we recommend Pinecone/Redis). Reranker invoked on top-N candidates, with cross-encoder run on dedicated batch capacity.

Open questions for Acme:
- Do you want automatic fallback to Dedicated reserved pool as a last resort, or prefer to keep Dedicated manual (ops-triggered)?
- What is the acceptable degradation window (e.g., allow p95 to go to 400ms for up to 5 minutes during incidents)?

I'll attach a draft YAML and sequence diagram to the Drive link; feel free to comment directly.

-Marcus
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>

Thanks team — Wed 11/25 worked well for the walkthrough, and the materials were helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infra folks after the session:

- Security asks for a short doc enumerating the audit log fields and retention options (can you share retention tiers and how to export logs to our SIEM?).
- Infra wants a recommended fallback cadence: they prefer automatic fallback to Dedicated only after 10 minutes of sustained breach, otherwise route to quantized model. Can you capture that in the draft YAML?
- For the reranker evaluation: we'll share a 500-sample set of queries by EOD Monday (Dec 1). Can you confirm Marcus/Dev will run the eval and push results to the shared Drive link?

Next steps agreed:
1) Redwood to update routing YAML with Dedicated-fallback-delay = 10m and cost guardrail thresholds.
2) Redwood to provide audit-log export options and retention table.
3) Acme to upload sample queries by 2026-12-01T17:00:00-08:00.

If you can send the updated YAML and audit doc as separate attachments by Tue 12/01 we can align on procurement/PO cadence in parallel.

Appreciate the clear sequencing — looking forward to the eval results.

-Sarah
Director, Product — Acme Corp
